svg.text: XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense → 8 PDM mics: wiring for Tier A + Tier B
One clock wire feeds all 8 mics. Each of the 4 data wires is shared by 2 mics (LEFT and RIGHT slot, chosen by the SEL pin).
Dot = connected. Wires that cross without a dot are not connected.
pins as seen from the underside (same view as your photo)
LiPo 3.7 V → BAT+ / BAT− pads on the underside. Charges
Snap-on Sense board: microSD (uses D8–D10), built-in test
mic (GPIO41/42, not on the edge pins), camera (unplug it).
Mics run from 3V3 only, never 5 V. All 8
Never leave it floating. LEFT mic → GND, RIGHT
mic → 3V3. The two mics on a line take turns
on the wire (one on the rising clock edge, one
One pin (D0) drives all 8 mics. Put the 33–100
Ω resistor right at D0. Keep each clock run
under ~30 cm and run a GND wire right next to
it. If the scope shows ringing, add a small
Tier A = the 4 LEFT mics (one per line). Tier
B = add the 4 RIGHT mics. No rewiring between
Wire and test one mic at a time: Mic 1 alone,
then its partner, then the next line. Label
D8–D10 (microSD). D2, D6, D7 stay spare for a
record button or a UART link.
Tap each mic to confirm the channel order in the buffer. If
hardware PCM conversion misbehaves with 4 lines, switch to RAW
format and decimate in software (like our pdm_decimator.c).
Red box = Tier A mic · Blue box = Tier B mic (positions from shirt-mic-layout.png)
